verdict.rationale: Nix ships an official, first-party CLI documented in its manual. It includes subcommands such as `nix develop`, `nix build`, `nix run`, `nix search`, `nix flake new`, `nix bundle` and `nix repl`, and community users confirm scripted use like `nix-shell --run`. One commenter's dislike of the CLI's ergonomics is opinion, not a functional contradiction. Missing for 10: documented agent-oriented affordances such as machine-readable (JSON) output or a non-interactive/automation mode guide.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: `nix develop` - run a bash shell that provides the build environment of a derivation
you can do `nix-shell --run "<some command>"`, and it will make sure you have all of the correct dependencies.
